audit.whatIsWrong: Every side token disagreed with the why printed under it. whys[0] says Sylas edges Level 1 but win[0] read Graves; whys[1] and whys[3] say 'neither owns the lane yet' and 'genuinely even' but both read Graves; whys[4] and whys[5] describe Graves kill windows but both read Skill; whys[6] hands the late game to Sylas but read Skill.
audit.why: The packet chart — Sylas / Skill / Graves / Skill / Graves / Graves / Sylas — matches the written reasoning exactly, and the 45.83% Emerald+ win rate over 72 games fits a lane Graves wins in two windows and loses either side of them.
audit.corrected: Chart set to the packet in both layers; the four boilerplate phase whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's phase whys were generic Graves text and never named a single Sylas ability — the packet's own defect line flags that the page 'never names any of Sylas's abilities'. Hijack's cooldown, the reason the late game is his, appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Hijack is 80/55/30s at 950 range. At rank 3 that is a 30-second cooldown on stealing Collateral Damage — he gets your ultimate roughly twice for every once you get it, which is the actual late-game story.
audit.corrected: Chain Lash, Kingslayer and Hijack named in the phase whys, with Hijack's 30s at rank 3 and Kingslayer's 6-12s stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications, each repeated four times. (a) Smoke Screen is used as a blind that makes his E recast 'whiff into the blind' — the ability has no blind, and a blind would not stop an ability in any case. (b) Collateral Damage is described as a wall-escape: 'firing it at a wall is your clean escape', 'R into a wall is also your get-out', 'Save R as a wall-escape'. Graves' R does not move him.
audit.why: Graves W: 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range... Move Speed reduced briefly.' Graves R: 'fires an explosive shell dealing heavy damage to the first champion it hits. After hitting a champion or reaching the end of its range, the shell explodes dealing damage in a cone.' No displacement, no self-movement.
audit.corrected: The smoke's real value restated — the sight-range cut is what stops him aiming the E recast — and every 'R as escape' line replaced with the correct use: hold it until both his 400-range dashes are spent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Abscond/Abduct is described purely as 'the dash that stuns' and as something that lands on you.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Sylas dashes to a location. Sylas can recast the ability to throw his chains out, pulling himself to an enemy he hits.' The recast pulls SYLAS to you — it is his re-engage, which is exactly why spending it is the green light for a Graves who wants him with no gap-closer left. 400 range, 13/12/11/10/9s.
audit.corrected: Described as a dash plus a chain re-engage, with range and cooldown, in the cooldown block, dosFull[0], report[5] and early. I did not assert or deny the recast's stun: Riot's text does not mention one, so I left that claim untouched rather than guess.

edits.before: Sylas is squishy and short-ranged until his E chain-dash, so level 1 you both poke with autos and he edges it with his Q drain-and-detonate while you have one ability and no E mobility to weave in. The lane turns at 2-3: once you've banked a second E charge and W is up, dash in for the point-blank 4-shell spread, and hold Smoke Screen to blind the SECOND cast of his E — the dash that stuns — so he eats your burst with no follow-up. Dodge the recast, not the first dash; the first cast is just travel toward you, the second is the stun.
edits.after: Sylas is squishy and short-ranged until his E chain-dash, so level 1 you both poke with autos and he edges it with his Q drain-and-detonate while you have one ability and no E mobility to weave in. The lane turns at 2-3: once you've banked a second E charge and W is up, dash in for the point-blank 4-shell spread, and drop Smoke Screen where he lands — it does not blind, but the sight-range cut means he can't line up the recast that chains him back onto you. Respect the recast, not the first dash; the first cast is only travel.

edits.before: This is your window. Your True Grit armor/MR and stored E charges compound, and at 6 Collateral Damage turns an even trade into a kill — fire the shell onto him after he burns both E dashes so there's no gap-close left and the cone behind him catches anything. R into a wall is also your get-out if his E2 stun lands first. Force every all-in now while his Q-W drain heal is still small: bait the E recast, blind it with W, then Q-detonate and reload before he can fully channel his sustain.
edits.after: This is your window. Your True Grit armor/MR and stored E charges compound, and at 6 Collateral Damage turns an even trade into a kill — fire the shell onto him after he burns both E dashes so there's no gap-close left and the cone behind him catches anything. Don't plan on R as an escape: it deals damage and moves you nowhere. Force every all-in now while Kingslayer's heal is still small — bait the E recast, smoke his footing, then Q-detonate and reload before his sustain pays.

edits.before: Hold W and drop the blind on his E2 landing spot so his chain-dash stun misses, then E in for the point-blank 4-shell burst
edits.after: Drop W where he lands so the sight cut stops him aiming the E recast, then dash in for the point-blank 4-shell burst

edits.before: Save R as a wall-escape if his E2 stun catches you, or fire it onto him after he burns both E dashes to finish before his heal kicks in
edits.after: Fire R onto him only after both 400-range dashes are spent — it is a nuke, not an escape, and it never bails you out of his re-engage

notes: Two fabricated mechanics, each repeated four times across both layers: Smoke Screen as a blind that makes an ability whiff, and Collateral Damage as a wall-escape. Neither exists — Graves' R has no displacement at all, so 'save R as a wall-escape' is advice that gets a player killed while they are already caught. Both are now replaced with what the abilities actually do. The packet's own defect line was right that no Sylas ability was ever named in the full layer; Chain Lash, Kingslayer, Abscond/Abduct and Hijack now appear with real numbers. I deliberately did NOT touch the claim that the E recast stuns: Riot's text describes only a dash and a chain-pull, so I have neither asserted nor removed it — see unverified.
